core.title: Use a dot for lateral variation in artifact names
core.given: A planner is authoring or renaming an artifact name.
core.when: The name expresses a lateral variation: the same conceptual level as its aspect, differing in flavor, state, type or facet.
core.then: Mark the lateral variation with a dot: append the variant to the aspect name after a dot (aspect.variant).
prefer: Follow the illustrative pattern domain:aspect.variant, e.g. domain:aspect.variantA vs domain:aspect.variantB for two states of one aspect.
Use the dot suffix for a different flavor, state, type or facet of the same aspect.
avoid: Using a dot for something that is not at the same conceptual level (a deeper or different aspect).
Encoding a lateral variant with another separator or by inventing a new aspect name, which hides that the artifacts are variants of one aspect.
core.why: A dot signals that artifacts are variants of one aspect, so readers and tooling can tell flavor/state variants apart from different aspects or levels.
evidence: Each artifact name that expresses a flavor/state/type/facet of an aspect carries that variant after a dot.
Reviewer confirms dot-suffixed names really are lateral (same conceptual level), consistent with the separator semantics convention.
verification: Scope: the rule applies wherever a planner authors or renames an artifact name, independently of the file or artifact kind in which the name appears; it applies to a single variant name, and no existing sibling variant is required.
Variant kinds covered: flavor, state, type, facet; lateral means the same conceptual level as the aspect.

Whether a difference is lateral versus deeper or different is a semantic judgment (llm_judged): a mechanical check can verify dot separation, but confirmation that dot-suffixed names really are lateral rests with reviewer judgment, consistent with the separator-semantics convention; separator choice for non-lateral differences is out of scope here.

Change-based activation needs a phase (planning) observer and an artifact-name observer that detects added or renamed artifact names independently of the file in which the name appears; neither fact is emitted today (needs_new_observer).

The source declares no per-rule severity or disposition; concrete compliant exemplar names are realization-specific (carried in the realization's verifier detail) and form no part of the core obligation.

values: an artifact name expresses a lateral variant of an aspect without a dot

fires: A planner names an artifact that is a particular flavor, state, type or facet of an aspect, even if it is the only variant named so far.
A planner names artifacts for distinct states of one aspect (e.g. an active vs. a closed state).
A planner renames an artifact variant that currently uses a non-dot separator for a lateral difference.
doesNotFire: The name expresses a different, deeper or hierarchical level rather than a lateral variant of an aspect (separator choice is governed by separator semantics).
Work that does not author or rename any artifact name.

bunOnly.text: Canonical source examples of compliant lateral variants: 'sensory:gesture.raw vs sensory:gesture.tapped'; 'player:session.active vs player:session.closed'; 'match:config.duel vs match:config.team'.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete exemplar names from the originating project, with no stack-neutral equivalent; the core keeps only the illustrative aspect.variant pattern, and bun.json is delivered as the worked reference example.
Finding ids of a single rule are realization details (vocabulary notProfileKeys); the core keeps the llm_judged observability and describes the finding generically.

neutralityNotes: The convention is a planner-facing artifact-naming rule that was already stack-neutral in the frozen Bun rewrite: no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path appears in any agent-facing field, so given/when/then/why, prefer, avoid, evidence, fires and doesNotFire are reproduced verbatim and the core needs nothing from the structure profile (profileRequirements empty). Scope is file-independent: the rule applies wherever a planner authors or renames an artifact name, as given and core verification state. Only two pieces of content are realization-only: the project-specific exemplar names (verifier_detail[0], kept because bun.json is the delivered reference example) and the checker's finding id (activation.facts[3]); the core substitutes an illustrative aspect.variant pattern and a generic finding description. The 'domain:' prefix in prefer[0] is an illustrative placeholder for the stack's aspect-name shape, not an obligation of this rule: separator choice outside the lateral suffix is governed by the separate separator-semantics convention. Activation notes about missing observers (phase, artifact-name) are preserved through the observability fields and the core's verification entries; the source declares no per-rule severity or disposition.
